flags: Partial overview: no cached designating, byway or tourism body verifies the catalog State Scenic Backway designation or states its rationale. Do not publish that designation as established. SR 79 eligibility is distinct from designation and from this corridor.

The cache gives no Ramona Expressway construction history, road geometry, through-driving time or complete endpoint description. The overview uses the documented parkway proposal as road-change history and the supplied west-to-east strip order for the journey.
The Mid County Parkway source describes a proposal and a completed interchange, not a completed through highway; no current construction or access claim is made.
The current Anza dates differ in the cache: Bautista Creek says 1774 and 1776, while San Jacinto Valley says 1774 and 1775. Omitted from Valle Vista pending an authoritative expedition source.

All current factual claims otherwise have cache support; supported agriculture, dairies, city layout, incorporation, hot-springs tourism and Ramona Pageant history were omitted to focus on the road and selected moments.

Indigenous history differs in emphasis and names between the city and valley articles; no tribal-authored cache is available. Broader settlement accounts are omitted rather than merging Luiseño, Serrano and Cahuilla histories.

All current moments and existing coordinates are retained. The flight marker has no current coordinates and no dedicated Wikipedia coordinates line, so none is invented. Current motifs keys are absent.

The cache records erection of the Cottonwood Avenue stone marker but does not explicitly confirm that specific marker still stands or current visitor access. Historical wording replaces the current draft’s present-tense marker claim. The overview is intentionally below 200 words because route-level evidence is incomplete.
